<description>
{
 "summary": "Fixes script decompression when handling oversized scripts by reassigning the target script to an OP_RETURN script rather than appending OP_RETURN to it. It also adds a unit test verifying that decompressing an oversized script into a reused destination containing an incomplete push results in an unspendable script.",
 "problem": "When decoding an oversized compressed script into an existing CScript buffer, operator<< appends OP_RETURN rather than replacing the buffer contents. If the destination buffer is reused and contains an unfinished push, the appended OP_RETURN byte is interpreted as push data instead of an unspendable opcode, potentially leaving the resulting script spendable.",
 "evidence": [
  "Author note in PR description: 'Found while reviewing #36280. This predates that PR and appears latent because oversized outputs are excluded from the UTXO set, but it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination.'",
  "Commit 11494efb01 adds a unit test showing that decompressing into a script with an incomplete push '0x01' resulted in an append that failed IsUnspendable()."

<category name="tools" title="Tools and scripts">
## Covers

Command-line tools other than the node and its RPC client, and the
scripts under contrib: `bitcoin-tx`, `bitcoin-util`, the offline
`bitcoin-wallet` tool, the `bitcoin` wrapper, seed and asmap
generation, signet tooling, tracing scripts, and developer helper
scripts. Build and release scripts are build; test helpers are tests.
The Scripts and tools label is a strong prior.

## What matters here

Tools that operators and downstream projects depend on first: seed
generation, asmap, signet, and the wallet tool affect real deployments.
Then correctness of any tool that touches keys or transactions. Then
developer productivity tools that many contributors use. Then niche or
single-user scripts, which rank low regardless of size.
